title: R18 certifies nonconstant dodecagonal Gaussian phase
problem: R16 derived a limiting phase function for the regular dodecagonal walk, but its phase values were proxies. The open question was whether the function is nonconstant.
failure: Floating phase samples or a numerical Bessel mean do not establish nonconstancy of an infinite sum.
correction: Compare the function at t=1 and t=sqrt(lambda), with lambda=sqrt(2+sqrt(3)). A common summable envelope bounds the omitted lattice tail, and rational interval bounds certify F(1)-F(sqrt(lambda))>1/10000.
transfer: For nonconstancy of an infinite lattice sum, choose two explicit parameter values, bound both tails with one summable envelope, and certify the finite comparison outward with exact intervals.
limits: Applies to the stated dodecagonal Gaussian phase function. The conclusion depends on R16's local-limit identification of this function with the walk observable. It does not prove period minimality, extrema, physical interpretation, or novelty. HORUS review is model-side, not human peer review.
